newsitem.title: UK: FTA protests air cargo surcharge, seeks dialogue.
newsitem.headline: FTA protests air cargo surcharge, seeks dialogue.

text.p: Britain's Freight Transport Association (FTA) has written to key airlines operating out of Britain formally protesting against the way in which air cargo fuel surcharges for air cargo were announced and introduced, an FTA official told Reuters.
"We're trying to get a better idea of how they arrived at their decision. We need to avoid this happening in the future and that means a dialogue," said FTA's Andrew Traill.
The airlines involved include British Airways World Cargo, KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV, Lufthansa Cargo, Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd and Emirates.

Many airlines providing cargo capacity out of Britain followed BA's lead and introduced fuel surcharges during November of six pence a kg for international routes and three pence a kg for European routes. This followed sharp rises in the price of jet fuel.

Traill added: "The FTA is very keen to change the attitude and mindset of airlines. Just because there is a sudden increase in costs, it does not mean, there should be sudden price rises. It's just not the way to do business."
The way the surcharges were introduced and in particular the lack of notice, varying in most cases between 10 days to three weeks caused, "a lot of ill-feeling, anger and frustration," he said.
"The whole industry will suffer if similar changes are made in this way," he added.
"We also hopeful that the UK AirFreight Forum will provide the right avenue for exploring the possibility of avoiding this situation in the future," Traill said.

The Forum, which groups airlines, airfreight forwarders and shippers, held its first meeting on November 5. It is designed a common meeting ground area where mutual problems can be discussed, industry sources said. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
